description: Historical seat of the Wadiyar dynasty, renowned for Indo-Saracenic grandeur, exquisite durbar halls, and evening illumination.

accessibility_notes.value: Wheelchairs available on site; ramp access provided to ground floor halls.

description: UNESCO World Heritage site and capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, situated among boulder-strewn hills along the Tungabhadra River.

accessibility_notes.value: Uneven stone pathways; moderate climbing required for surrounding monuments.

safety_info.ghat_road_advisory: Avoid night driving on ghat sections

description: Sixth-century rock-cut cave temples of the Chalukya dynasty overlooking the tranquil Agastya Lake.

accessibility_notes.value: Rock-cut stairs to upper caves; difficult for visitors with restricted mobility.

description: UNESCO World Heritage site representing the harmonious synthesis of northern Rekha-Nagara and southern Dravida architectural styles.

accessibility_notes.value: Flat lawn complex with paved walkways between temples.

description: Celebrated as the cradle of Hindu rock temple architecture, featuring an unusual apsidal sanctum.

accessibility_notes.value: Ground-level garden with stone plinths.

description: Heart of the Kodagu coffee country with rolling hill views, mist, and the historical 17th-century palace fort.

accessibility_notes.value: Raja's seat garden is paved; fort ramparts have stepped inclines.

description: Highest peak in Karnataka (1,930 m) offering sweeping vistas of the Western Ghats and trek paths.

accessibility_notes.value: Requires climbing approx 450 stone steps from vehicle stop to summit.

description: Coastal pilgrimage hub featuring ancient Atma Linga shrine and natural Om-shaped cliff beaches.

accessibility_notes.value: Temple town has narrow lanes; cliff paths between beaches require walking.

safety_info.ghat_road_advisory: Avoid night driving on ghat sections

name_kn: ಉಡುಪಿ ಶ್ರೀ ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಮಠ ಮತ್ತು ಮಲ್ಪೆ
description: 13th-century Vaishnavite monastery founded by Saint Madhvacharya, famed for Kanakana Kindi and coastal Udupi cuisine.

accessibility_notes.value: Main temple entrance has accessible ramps; dining halls have ground seating.

description: Colossal 123-foot Lord Shiva statue and 20-story Raja Gopura surrounded on three sides by the Arabian Sea.

accessibility_notes.value: Lift facility available inside the Raja Gopura to view the coastline.

description: Majestic segmented plunge waterfalls formed by the Sharavathi River, dropping 253 meters in four cascades: Raja, Roarer, Rocket, and Rani.

accessibility_notes.value: Main viewing gallery is paved and wheelchair friendly.

safety_info.ghat_road_advisory: Avoid night driving on ghat sections

description: UNESCO World Heritage site representing the pinnacle of Hoysala stone sculpture, commissioned by King Vishnuvardhana in 1117 CE.

accessibility_notes.value: Raised star-shaped soapstone plinth requires climbing ~8 stone steps.

description: Twin-sanctum Hoysala masterpiece covered in intricate stone friezes illustrating epics, mythology, and 12th-century life.

accessibility_notes.value: Grounds and garden pathways are level; steps onto the outer platform.

description: 57-foot monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali carved in 981 CE atop Vindhyagiri hill, a venerated Jain pilgrimage destination.

accessibility_notes.value: Climb of 650 rock-cut steps; palanquin (doli) service available for elders.

description: Historic 240-acre botanical garden founded by Hyder Ali featuring the iconic Glass House and rare century-old trees.

accessibility_notes.value: Paved flat paths, electric buggies available for seniors and persons with disabilities.

description: First of four cardinal monasteries established by Adi Shankaracharya on the banks of Tunga River, renowned for the zodiac stone pillars of Vidyashankara temple.

accessibility_notes.value: Riverside complex has paved concourses and gentle ramps into temple courtyards.

description: Dense Western Ghats reserve offering whitewater rafting on the Kali River, hornbill birding, and jungle safari.

accessibility_notes.value: River rafting and forest trails require good physical mobility.

safety_info.ghat_road_advisory: Avoid night driving on ghat sections

description: Coastal port city celebrated for pristine beaches, Gokanatheshwara temple, and unique Tulu Nadu gastronomy (Ghee Roast, Neer Dosa).

accessibility_notes.value: Panambur promenade has level pedestrian access.

description: Mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah boasting one of the world's largest unsupported acoustic domes and whispering gallery.

accessibility_notes.value: Ground floor is accessible; whispering gallery requires climbing narrow spiral staircases.

description: Premier wildlife sanctuary famous for dense leopard and tiger sightings, elephant herds, and boat safaris along the backwaters.

accessibility_notes.value: Safari vehicles require stepping up onto open jeep/canter frames.

description: Formidable stone fortress with seven concentric defensive walls, 19 gateways, 38 postern gates, and ancient rainwater harvesting tanks.

accessibility_notes.value: Extensive uphill walking on uneven rock slopes.

description: Twin cascading waterfalls on the Kaveri River, location of India's first major hydroelectric station (built 1902).

accessibility_notes.value: Viewpoints feature fenced stone walkways; Barachukki has stairs down toward the basin.

description: UNESCO World Heritage site (2023) trikuta (triple-shrine) temple built in 1268 CE, fully enclosed by a pillared cloister.

accessibility_notes.value: Well-kept level lawn surrounding the temple platform.

description: Distinctive horse-face shaped mountain peak surrounded by rolling shola grasslands and evergreen rainforests.

accessibility_notes.value: Steep 9 km mountain trek requiring forest department permission; strictly for fit trekkers.

safety_info.ghat_road_advisory: Avoid night driving on ghat sections

description: Massive 15th-century Bahmani Sultanate fort spanning over 5 km of perimeter walls, enclosing the ancient capital city with its distinctive Persian-style gateways and water supply system.

accessibility_notes.value: Uneven fort terrain; some areas require climbing.

description: 13th-century Sufi saint's dargah considered sacred by both Hindus and Muslims, drawing devotees in a unique tradition of communal harmony.

accessibility_notes.value: Mosque and dargah complex has paved walkways.

description: Graceful 17th-century mausoleum of Ibrahim Adil Shah II, noted for its delicate stone lacework and considered an architectural precursor of the Taj Mahal.

accessibility_notes.value: Well-maintained garden grounds; platform steps at mausoleum entrance.

description: A pair of identical domed mausoleums built in the Adil Shahi architectural tradition, standing as lesser-known gems in Bijapur's monument cluster.

accessibility_notes.value: Open grounds; no steps to main structures.

description: 14th-century Bahmani fort housing the Jama Masjid, one of the earliest mosques in India built with an arched roof inspired by the Cordoba mosque in Spain.

accessibility_notes.value: Flat courtyard approach; some uneven surfaces inside.

description: River island fortress-town that served as Tipu Sultan's capital, home to the ancient Ranganathaswamy temple, Tipu's summer palace Dariya Daulat, and the fort walls.

accessibility_notes.value: Flat island terrain; museum interiors accessible.

description: Terraced Mughal-style garden downstream of the Krishnaraja Sagara Dam, famous for musical fountain illumination shows in the evenings.

accessibility_notes.value: Terraced gardens have steps between levels; main lawn paths are paved.

description: Ancient Shiva temple on the banks of the Kapila River, one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in Karnataka with a 40-metre Dravidian gopura.

accessibility_notes.value: Main shrine corridor has stone floors; accessible approach to outer courtyard.

description: 12th-century Vaishnavite temple on a rocky hillock reformulated by the philosopher-saint Ramanuja, famous for its Vairamudi festival when the deity is adorned with a diamond crown.

accessibility_notes.value: Rocky hill approach with stone steps; challenging for reduced mobility visitors.

description: Ancient temple town on the Kaveri River where medieval Ganga-dynasty temples lie partially buried under sand dunes, with Vaidyeshwara temple as the main active shrine.

accessibility_notes.value: Sand terrain; some temples excavated and accessible with steps.

description: Geologically protected cluster of four islands off Malpe beach, famous for the distinctive hexagonal basalt columns formed by ancient volcanic activity, accessible only by ferry.

accessibility_notes.value: Ferry access required; rocky basalt surfaces on islands.

description: Secluded crescent-shaped beach south of Gokarna town, accessible by a short cliff trek, offering calm waters and a quieter alternative to Om Beach.

accessibility_notes.value: Narrow cliff path access; not suitable for reduced mobility visitors.

description: 16th-century laterite fort built by the Nawabs of Savanur on the Aganashini River estuary, now lush with vegetation and noted for birdwatching in its moat.

accessibility_notes.value: Grass-covered ramparts; mostly flat interior grounds.

description: Wide sandy beach adjacent to the Murdeshwar temple complex on Kanduka Hill, offering views of the Shiva statue from the shoreline and calm waters for wading.

accessibility_notes.value: Open beach with level sand access.

description: Western Ghats village known as the Cherrapunji of the South, with a celebrated sunset viewpoint overlooking the Someshwara valley and serving as a king cobra research site.

accessibility_notes.value: Short walk to sunset viewpoint; forest trails require sturdy footwear.

description: 70-foot waterfall surrounded by coffee plantation estates and spice gardens, accessible via a short forest walk from Madikeri.

accessibility_notes.value: Paved viewing platform; steep steps down to closer viewpoint.

description: Forest department elephant camp on an island in the Kaveri River where visitors can observe elephant bathing and feeding; Karnataka Forest Department managed.

accessibility_notes.value: River crossing by coracle required; riverbank terrain.

description: Project Tiger reserve in the Bhadra river basin with dense deciduous forest, home to tigers, leopards, gaur, and over 250 species of birds.

accessibility_notes.value: Safari jeep access; not suitable for visitors with limited mobility.

description: Scenic heritage railway trail through Western Ghats tunnels and viaducts from Sakleshpur towards Subramanya, passing through dense rainforest and offering panoramic valley views.

accessibility_notes.value: Requires crossing active railway tracks; sturdy trekking footwear essential.

description: India's first dedicated sloth bear sanctuary near Hampi, where over 120 free-ranging sloth bears can be observed from an elevated watch tower in their natural rocky habitat.

accessibility_notes.value: Paved path to watch tower; steps up to observation deck.

description: Gravity-cum-masonry dam built across the Tungabhadra River in 1953, with a terraced garden, rowing facilities, and panoramic views of the backwaters.

accessibility_notes.value: Flat approach to dam crest viewpoint; garden paths are paved.

description: Ancient settlement across the Tungabhadra from Hampi, believed to be the mythological Kishkinda of the Ramayana, featuring Anjaneya Hill, Pampa Sarovar, and traditional village life.

accessibility_notes.value: Village paths; Anjaneya Hill requires 575 steps.

description: One of Asia's largest monolithic hills at 1,226 m, rising dramatically from the Deccan plain with ancient fort ruins atop and trekking routes of varying difficulty.

accessibility_notes.value: Steep rock face climb; requires physical fitness; guide recommended.

description: One of India's premier Project Tiger reserves at the tri-state junction of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala, with large populations of elephants, tigers, leopards, and wild dogs.

accessibility_notes.value: Safari canter and jeep access from gate; not suitable for visitors with limited mobility.

description: Dramatic black crystalline karst rock formations rising 120 m from dense forest, with the two main peaks named Bhairaveshwara Shikhara and Mohini Shikhara, housing ancient shrines.

accessibility_notes.value: Forest walk to rocks; steep scramble to upper shrine areas.

description: Hill fortress at 1,478 m, once Tipu Sultan's summer retreat, offering spectacular sunrise views and the base for one of Karnataka's most popular cycling climbs.

accessibility_notes.value: Paved road to summit; garden walkways are accessible; some viewpoints involve short steep paths.

description: Iconic Vittala Temple complex housing the famous stone chariot and musical pillars, the finest example of Vijayanagara architecture within the UNESCO World Heritage Hampi site.

accessibility_notes.value: Footwear must be removed; paved courtyard approach.

description: Medieval hilltop fort that changed hands between the Bahmani Sultanate, Vijayanagara Empire, and Adil Shahis, offering panoramic views of the Deccan plains from its 300 m elevation.

accessibility_notes.value: Steep climb to fort; rocky terrain.

description: Village famed for its cluster of Chalukya-era temples and stepped wells (kalyanis), with the Kashi Vishveshvara temple showcasing ornate stonework and lathe-turned pillars.

accessibility_notes.value: unknown

description: 12th-century Chalukya temple dedicated to Shiva with three lingas, noted for its elaborately carved pillars, ornate doorways, and the attached Saraswati shrine with finely detailed figure work.

accessibility_notes.value: unknown

description: Hill fort overlooking Yadgir town and the Krishna river valley, historically a strategic stronghold of the Bahmani and Adil Shahi periods, with gateways and ruined bastions.

accessibility_notes.value: unknown

description: Temple village home to the Mahadeva temple and an ancient step well (kalyani), part of the Kuknoor group of Chalukya monuments near Hampi.

accessibility_notes.value: unknown

description: 12th-century Hoysala temple at Koravangala village, raised on the classic star-shaped Jagati platform with lathe-turned pillars and richly carved ceilings and deities.

description: Beach whose shoreline curves into the shape of the Sanskrit 'Om' symbol, one of Gokarna's most popular beaches with shacks, beach trekking, and water sports.

accessibility_notes.value: unknown

description: Coastal stretch along the Kali river estuary with the Tagore Beach promenade and museum, palm-lined sands, and views of the Arabian Sea; the beach is named after Rabindranath Tagore, who visited the town.

description: Hill fortress east of Tumakuru with successive fort tiers, the Yoga Narasimha temple near the summit, the Bhoganandishwara temple at its base, and panoramic ridge views.

description: Volcanic rock hillock near Kolar with a perennial spring feeding the Someshwara (Antharagange) temple, popular for cave exploration and a short night trek from Bengaluru.

accessibility_notes.value: unknown

accessibility_notes.value: unknown

description: Scenic area around the Manchanabele reservoir near Magadi, known for birdwatching, kayaking, and the nearby rocky gorges, popular for quick day-trips from Bengaluru.

description: India's first modern gurukul for Indian classical dance, founded by Protima Gauri Bedi near Hesaraghatta, where resident dancers train in styles such as Odissi in a village designed by architect Gerard da Cunha.
